extracted.intended_audience: graduate students applying for NIH NRSA Individual Predoctoral (F31) fellowships / applicants and their mentors
extracted.subtask_short: NIH F31 NRSA predoctoral fellowship application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and required components for preparing and submitting an NIH NRSA Individual Predoctoral Fellowship (Parent F31) application, including project narrative, specific aims, training plan, institutional commitment, facilities, human/animal subjects disclosures, and required certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA instructions for application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample cautions that although it demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed and applicants must follow their FOA's instructions; NIAID posts new samples periodically (https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF 424 (R&R) form fields and institutional identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all required SF 424 (R&R) application fields including type of submission, dates, applicant legal name, department, contact person, EIN/TIN, DUNS, type of applicant, type of application (New/Resubmission/Continuation), federal funding requested, and congressional district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The application must include administrative data on the SF424 cover page and related contact/authorized representative information so the agency can route, process, and validate the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and assurances / signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing this application, the signer certifies to the statements contained in the list of certifications and assurances and agrees to comply with any resulting terms if an award is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signer acknowledges that false statements may subject them to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001); the list of certifications/assurances is contained in the announcement or agency-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required application components (Table of Contents items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must include the listed components (e.g., SF 424 R&R Cover Page; Project Summary/Abstract; Project Narrative; Bibliography & References Cited; Facilities & Other Resources; Equipment; Research & Related Senior/Key Person; PHS Fellowship Supplemental; Applicant's Background & Goals for Fellowship Training; Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Sponsor/Co-sponsor Statements; Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research; Letters of Support; Description of Institutional Environment and Commitment to Training; Resource Sharing Plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Table of Contents in the sample enumerates the sections reviewers and agency staff expect to find—omitting or misplacing sections may render the application incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary / Abstract must state significance, hypothesis, and specific aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Summary/Abstract should summarize the scientific problem, its significance, the hypothesis, preliminary data context, and clearly state the Specific Aims (e.g., Aim 1, Aim 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Project Summary describes biological background, knowledge gaps, preliminary findings, hypothesis that dsRNAs contain competing OAS1 binding sites, and lists two specific aims to address the question; summaries should be concise and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative must describe public health relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief Project Narrative explaining why the research is relevant to public health (e.g., understanding innate immune regulation and potential to design antiviral treatments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Narrative statements should make plain the potential health impact and translational importance of the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims section required
rubrics_metrics.description: A Specific Aims page that clearly enumerates the project objectives (e.g., Aim 1: determine dsRNA features that lead to potent activation of OAS1; Aim 2: define molecular mechanisms using biochemical/biophysical/structural approaches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims should be focused, testable, and aligned with the Research Strategy and summary; reviewers often evaluate clarity and feasibility of the aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy / Research Plan content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Research Strategy describing methods, complementary assays (in vitro and in human cells), biochemical, biophysical, and structural approaches, and experimental rationale and feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample emphasizes complementary assays and multiple approaches; the Research Strategy should justify experimental choices, address potential pitfalls, and align with aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include PHS Fellowship Supplemental materials as required for NRSA F31 submissions (e.g., training plan, sponsor statements, sponsor and co-sponsor contributions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PHS Fellowship Supplemental provides fellowship-specific details (mentorship, training timeline, sponsor responsibilities) that reviewers use to judge training potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's Background and Goals for Fellowship Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an Applicant's Background and Goals for Fellowship Training section documenting prior experience, training goals, and how the fellowship will advance the applicant's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section should make a persuasive case for why the candidate needs the fellowship and how planned activities will address gaps in training toward the stated career goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects involvement disclosure and IRB documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer 'Are Human Subjects Involved?' If YES, state whether the project is exempt (and exemption number) or whether IRB review is pending or approved, and provide IRB approval date and assurance number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must fully disclose human subjects involvement and include necessary IRB approvals or justification for exemption; failure to provide accurate human subjects info can prevent funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals involvement disclosure and IACUC documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer 'Are Vertebrate Animals Used?' If YES, indicate whether IACUC review is pending or approved and provide IACUC approval date and animal welfare assurance number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete vertebrate animal sections with required oversight information; compliance with institutional animal welfare assurance is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary/privileged information and environmental/historic impact disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether proprietary/privileged information is included; answer if the project has actual or potential environmental impact and whether it involves a site designated (or eligible) as a historic place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanations where requested; environmental assessments (EA/EIS) or exemptions may be required for projects with environmental impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign activities disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether the project involves activities outside the United States or partnerships with international collaborators and identify countries if yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign site/collaboration information must be transparent; some FOAs require additional approvals or documentation for international work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources: describe intellectual environment and physical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the institutional and departmental intellectual environment, access to colleagues, seminars, lab meetings, and the physical laboratory resources (bench space, storage, biosafety level, specialized rooms such as hot labs or crystallography areas), and confirmation of biosafety and radiation safety training/approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample gives detailed descriptions of lab space, BSL-2 approval, specialized instrumentation, and training completion; reviewers assess whether the environment and resources are adequate to accomplish the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment: list essential equipment and core facility access
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an Equipment section documenting instruments and platforms available to the project (e.g., FPLC systems, plate readers, UV/Vis spectrophotometers, crystallization incubators) and access to institutional core facilities (e.g., genomics core, HDX-MS, OctetRED384, APS beamtime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenting specific equipment and immediate access demonstrates feasibility; mention shared/core facility logistics and proximity where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional support / Commitment to training
rubrics_metrics.description: Document institutional commitment and support for trainee development, including mentorship plans, thesis committee composition, institutional courses and seminars, opportunities for presenting and receiving feedback, and availability of professional development resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample details mentor and co-mentor roles, committee members, seminar series, and LGS/BCDB program supports; reviewers evaluate strength of institutional training environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Structure and Required Milestones (coursework, rotations, teaching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe program requirements and timing: core coursework completion by end of Spring Year 2, three 10-week research rotations in Year 1, teaching assistantship/teaching training, and elective options. Specify milestones and expected timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly lay out curricula and timelines so reviewers can assess whether trainee will complete necessary milestones during the fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching requirement and training (TATTO/TATT 600)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document required teaching training: participation in the Teaching Assistant Training and Teaching Opportunity (TATTO) Program, completion of a 2-day teaching training workshop (TATT 600), and serving as a Teaching Assistant for at least one semester with evaluation via course director reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain planned teaching activities and how quality of teaching will be evaluated; some programs require specific training modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifying Exams (QE1 and QE2) requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: State Qualifying Exam structure and timing: QE1 is a written (essay-type), closed-book exam administered over two days to test foundational knowledge (typically May/June Year 1); QE2 is an oral examination (to be completed before June 1 of Year 2) assessing integration of training, research design, data interpretation, and presentation skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain when QEs will be taken and how they fit into the training timeline; meeting QE milestones is required to progress in the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissertation defense prerequisites and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a dissertation defense is scheduled the student must produce a rigorous body of novel research including at least one first-author peer-reviewed research paper published or accepted; the defense process requires (i) submission of the written dissertation, (ii) a closed-session oral examination by the thesis committee, and (iii) an advertised public oral presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear the publication expectation and sequential steps for defense; reviewers look for feasible plans to meet these prerequisites during the fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, evaluation, and committee meeting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Student progress is monitored via formal processes including academic probation rules (based on coursework grades/GPA); dissertation committees must be formed after QE1, hold the first meeting no later than six months after passing QE2; continuing meetings are required every six months (every four months after Year 5). Committee meeting presentations must include specified slides (scientific update, short-term goals, goals beyond graduate school).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented monitoring plans, meeting frequency, and reporting formats demonstrate structured oversight and accountability for trainee progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan aligned with NIH and institutional policies
rubrics_metrics.description: All reagents produced during the research will be shared in line with Emory University and NIH policies; data will be shared with collaborators and through publications, and where appropriate deposited in public repositories (e.g., RCSB Protein Data Bank for structure coordinates and maps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit commitments to share materials and data, and specify repositories and timing; resource sharing plans are evaluated for reasonableness and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA and confidentiality notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are warned that when NIH responds to FOIA requests, materials will be subject to FOIA exemptions and substantial redactions; NIH must protect confidential commercial or financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that portions of the application may be disclosed under FOIA with appropriate redactions; this affects how proprietary information is presented and what must be clearly labelled as privileged.
